description: SET XACT_ABORT ON IS NOT SUPPORTED IN SNOWFLAKE.
problem_description: The T-SQL session statement `SET XACT_ABORT ON` has no equivalent in Snowflake Scripting, so SnowConvert emits SSC-EWI-TS0089 and comments the statement out. In SQL Server, `SET XACT_ABORT ON` makes the engine abort the whole batch and roll back the entire open transaction whenever a run-time statement raises an error, instead of failing only the offending statement. Snowflake has no such session option: it uses autocommit by default, and inside an explicit `BEGIN TRANSACTION` block a statement error does not by itself roll back the transaction - the transaction stays open until it is explicitly committed or rolled back, or until the session ends. Because the directive is dropped, a procedure such as `etl.usp_Load_SalesDW` that relied on `SET XACT_ABORT ON` for all-or-nothing behaviour loses its automatic rollback-on-error guarantee, so a mid-run failure can leave the target tables (DimDate, DimProduct, DimCustomer, FactSales) partially loaded even though the original procedure would have rolled everything back. The related `IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK` in the CATCH block also has no direct Snowflake counterpart and must be reworked together with it.
